QAuth's [SSF transmitter](/operate/ssf-transmitter/) sends the events that record a security
change to receivers' streams, as Security Event Tokens (SETs, RFC 8417). Each is sent as a CAEP 1.0
or RISC 1.0 event where one says the same thing, and as a QAuth-defined event where none does.
Resource servers and relying parties use them to stop honouring a revoked session, grant or
credential before its tokens expire ([ADR-019 Decision 8](/reference/records/adr/019-deployment-topology-and-trust-boundaries/)).

The [event registry](/reference/events/) marks every type that records a security change: a
session, a grant, a token, a credential, a key or an account that a receiver may have to act on.
Each security type declares the SSF event it is sent as, or that it has none; the registry's test
fails when one declares neither, so no feature adds a security event and forgets SSF. This page is
generated from those declarations.

## The SET

A SET carries one event and these claims:

- `iss`: the realm's issuer; `aud`: the receiver's `client_id`.
- `jti`: the event's id, and `iat`: the event's time, in seconds. A retry sends the same SET,
  so a receiver drops a duplicate by its `jti`.
- `sub_id`: the subject (SSF 1.0 §3, RFC 9493), as below.
- `events`: one member, keyed by the SSF event's URI.

It carries no `sub` and no `exp` (SSF 1.0 §4.1.2, §4.1.7). Its header names the signing key
(`kid`) and `typ: secevent+jwt`; the keys are at the transmitter's `jwks_uri`.

## Common members

Every mapped event carries `event_timestamp`, the time the event happened in seconds (CAEP
1.0 §2). It carries `initiating_entity` when QAuth knows who invoked it: `user` for a person acting on their own account, `admin` for an administrator (a person acting on an admin event, or an operator on the server host), and `system` for QAuth itself. A client acting for itself names none.
A mapping may fix it instead, as the replay policy does.

## Subjects

- A user is `iss_sub`: the realm's issuer and the user's id.
- A client is `uri` when its `client_id` is an absolute URI, as an agent client's Client ID
  Metadata Document URL is, and `opaque` with the `client_id` otherwise.
- A key is `opaque` with its `kid`.

The transmitter's `default_subjects` is `NONE`: a stream receives an event only when it
requested the event and its receiver added the subject, except an event about a key, which every
stream of the realm that requested it receives. An event marked as going to the event's client
reaches only the stream whose receiver is that client: it tells of the user's dealings with that
one client, which another receiver has no need to see.

A receiver may add a user only when the user is related to the receiver's client: the user has an
active consent for it, or holds a live refresh token it was issued. Any other user, and a user id
that does not exist, is refused with `403`, as SSF 1.0 §8.1.3.2 prescribes for a subject the
receiver may not add. So the receiver is the client the users sign in through, given the
`client_credentials` grant and the `ssf:stream` scope as well: a client of its own, which no
user signs in to, can add no user. The relation is checked when the subject is added; the subject
then stays on the stream until the receiver removes it, also after the user withdraws the consent
or the refresh token ends.

## Mapping

| QAuth event type                                                          | SSF event                                                 | Subject                               | Delivered to                                                | Members besides `event_timestamp`                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`user.signed_out`](/reference/events/#usersigned_out-v1-rc0)             | `session-revoked` (CAEP 1.0 §3.1)                         | the user, `iss_sub`                   | every stream that added the subject                         | `initiating_entity` from the actor                                                                                                                             |
| [`consent.revoked`](/reference/events/#consentrevoked-v1-rc0)             | `token-claims-change` (CAEP 1.0 §3.2)                     | the user, `iss_sub`                   | the stream of the event’s client, when it added the subject | `claims`: `{"scope":""}`; `initiating_entity` from the actor                                                                                                   |
| [`token.family_revoked`](/reference/events/#tokenfamily_revoked-v1-rc0)   | `session-revoked` (CAEP 1.0 §3.1)                         | the user, `iss_sub`                   | the stream of the event’s client, when it added the subject | `reason_admin`: by `data.reason`; `initiating_entity`: `"policy"`                                                                                              |
| [`token.revoked`](/reference/events/#tokenrevoked-v1-rc0)                 | [`token-revoked`](#token-revoked) (QAuth)                 | the user, `iss_sub`                   | the stream of the event’s client, when it added the subject | `token_type_hint`: `data.typeHint`; `initiating_entity` from the actor                                                                                         |
| [`client.secret_rotated`](/reference/events/#clientsecret_rotated-v1-rc0) | `credential-change` (CAEP 1.0 §3.3)                       | the client, `uri` or `opaque`         | the stream of the event’s client, when it added the subject | `credential_type`: `"client-secret"`; `change_type`: `"update"`; `initiating_entity`: `"admin"`                                                                |
| [`api_key.created`](/reference/events/#api_keycreated-v1-rc0)             | `credential-change` (CAEP 1.0 §3.3)                       | the event’s client, `uri` or `opaque` | the stream of the event’s client, when it added the subject | `credential_type`: `"api-key"`; `change_type`: `"create"`; `initiating_entity`: `"admin"`                                                                      |
| [`api_key.revoked`](/reference/events/#api_keyrevoked-v1-rc0)             | `credential-change` (CAEP 1.0 §3.3)                       | the event’s client, `uri` or `opaque` | the stream of the event’s client, when it added the subject | `credential_type`: `"api-key"`; `change_type`: `"revoke"`; `initiating_entity`: `"admin"`                                                                      |
| [`wallet.linked`](/reference/events/#walletlinked-v1-rc0)                 | `credential-change` (CAEP 1.0 §3.3)                       | the user, `iss_sub`                   | every stream that added the subject                         | `credential_type`: `"verifiable-credential"`; `change_type`: by `data.rebound` (`true` → `"update"`, `false` → `"create"`); `initiating_entity` from the actor |
| [`key.emergency_retired`](/reference/events/#keyemergency_retired-v1-rc0) | [`key-emergency-retired`](#key-emergency-retired) (QAuth) | the key, `opaque` with its `kid`      | every stream of the realm that requested it                 | `kid`: `data.keyId`; `purpose`: `data.purpose`; `initiating_entity` from the actor                                                                             |

Notes on the mapping:

- [`consent.revoked`](/reference/events/#consentrevoked-v1-rc0): A withdrawn consent covered every scope the client held for the user, so the `scope` of its tokens for that user is now empty, and QAuth revoked the refresh tokens the consent covered.
- [`token.family_revoked`](/reference/events/#tokenfamily_revoked-v1-rc0): A refresh family is the client’s standing session for the user, so its revocation is `session-revoked`. The replay policy revoked it, so `initiating_entity` is `policy`.
- [`token.revoked`](/reference/events/#tokenrevoked-v1-rc0): Sent only when the revoked token was a user’s: the event’s subject. A revocation that matched no token of the client records the event without one, and no stream receives it.
- [`client.secret_rotated`](/reference/events/#clientsecret_rotated-v1-rc0): Sent only to the stream of the client whose credential changed, never to another receiver that added that client: a receiver learns of its own credentials only. A developer managing a client acts as its administrator, so `initiating_entity` is `admin`.
- [`api_key.created`](/reference/events/#api_keycreated-v1-rc0): Sent only to the stream of the client whose credential changed, never to another receiver that added that client: a receiver learns of its own credentials only. A developer managing a client acts as its administrator, so `initiating_entity` is `admin`.
- [`api_key.revoked`](/reference/events/#api_keyrevoked-v1-rc0): Sent only to the stream of the client whose credential changed, never to another receiver that added that client: a receiver learns of its own credentials only. A developer managing a client acts as its administrator, so `initiating_entity` is `admin`.
- [`key.emergency_retired`](/reference/events/#keyemergency_retired-v1-rc0): Defined ahead of emergency retirement itself (#551), which emits it; nothing emits it before then.

## Security events with no SSF event

| QAuth event type                                                                | Why it has no SSF event                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`step_up.elevated`](/reference/events/#step_upelevated-v1-rc0)                 | CAEP 1.0 §3.4 `assurance-level-change` signals that the authentication method changed, and needs the level before and after in a namespace. QAuth’s step-up asks for a fresh sign-in with the same method and records no assurance level, so that event would say nothing true. It maps once step-up can raise the level, with passkeys or TOTP (ADR-018 §3). |
| [`client.deleted`](/reference/events/#clientdeleted-v1-rc0)                     | No CAEP 1.0 or RISC 1.0 event describes a client’s suspension or deletion: RISC `account-disabled` is about an account a person signs in to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`client.suspended`](/reference/events/#clientsuspended-v1-rc0)                 | No CAEP 1.0 or RISC 1.0 event describes a client’s suspension or deletion: RISC `account-disabled` is about an account a person signs in to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`client.suspension_lifted`](/reference/events/#clientsuspension_lifted-v1-rc0) | No CAEP 1.0 or RISC 1.0 event describes a client’s suspension or deletion: RISC `account-disabled` is about an account a person signs in to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

RISC 1.0 `account-disabled` and `account-enabled` map the disabling and enabling of a user,
which has no event type yet: they arrive with that feature, under the same rule.

## QAuth-defined events

Where no CAEP 1.0 or RISC 1.0 event says what happened, QAuth defines one. Its identifier is
`urn:qauth:secevent:<name>:v<N>`, a URN rather than a URL so that it never looks like a standard
event, and versioned so that a standard one can later sit beside it (ADR-018 §5). Until QAuth 1.0.0
every QAuth-defined identifier is a release candidate, `:v<N>-rc.<M>`, and nothing about it is
promised: a breaking change raises `<M>`. The release that ships 1.0.0 drops the suffix. A
receiver ignores members it does not know (SSF 1.0 §4.2.3).

### token-revoked

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:secevent:token-revoked:v1-rc.0`
- Sent for: [`token.revoked`](/reference/events/#tokenrevoked-v1-rc0)

A client revoked a token of the subject at the RFC 7009 revocation endpoint. The SET goes to the stream of that client only. QAuth defines it because no CAEP event matches: `session-revoked` would say the whole session ended, and `credential-change` is about a credential the subject authenticates with.

| Member              | Required | Meaning                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event_timestamp`   | yes      | When the event happened, in seconds since the epoch (CAEP 1.0 §2).                        |
| `initiating_entity` | no       | Who invoked it, as CAEP 1.0 §2 names it; see [Common members](#common-members).           |
| `token_type_hint`   | no       | The `token_type_hint` the client sent, such as `refresh_token`. Absent when it sent none. |

### key-emergency-retired

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:secevent:key-emergency-retired:v1-rc.0`
- Sent for: [`key.emergency_retired`](/reference/events/#keyemergency_retired-v1-rc0)

An operator retired a key of the realm that may be compromised (ADR-019 Decision 9). It left the JWKS at once and no verifier in the auth server accepts it. A verifier drops the key the SET names. The subject is the key, as an `opaque` identifier holding its `kid`, and every stream of the realm that requested the event receives it.

| Member              | Required | Meaning                                                                         |
| ------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event_timestamp`   | yes      | When the event happened, in seconds since the epoch (CAEP 1.0 §2).              |
| `initiating_entity` | no       | Who invoked it, as CAEP 1.0 §2 names it; see [Common members](#common-members). |
| `kid`               | yes      | The `kid` of the retired key.                                                   |
| `purpose`           | no       | What the key was for, such as `token_signing`.                                  |
